comment.content:
I think both of these approaches share some flaws. The whole concept of "-maxxxing" implies both that there are objectively good and bad things to be, and implies that more = better. Also, in this context both of these things are being performed for the sake of others rather than the self. 

I would say that there are some personality traits that are objectively bad and should be avoided. There are some personality traits that I can say I like tbe peoplr I interact with to have, but I have a hard time saying someone objectively wrong for not having those. 

There was a period of my life where I pretended to be extroverted. I learned a bunch of stuff and consumed a bunch of media, not because of genuine self interest but so that I would have stuff to talk about at parties. I became an interesting person for the sake of being seen by others as interesting. It was exhausting. Eventually I was honest with myself, stopped putting on that performance for others, and embraced being "boring". That led to me being a lot more satisfied with the things I did enjoy doing, and a lot happier overall.

The End.
